target: new: coloured marking (colour + pattern): white (PATO_0000323) and streaked (FLOPO:0991206)
reason: Two values joined: the colour white and a striped pattern. PATO 'striped' is only a RELATED synonym of banded, which means transverse bands. A pattern that ties the colour to the marking avoids a new class for every colour.
This means few-flowered: a count of flowers (bearer: flower, container: inflorescence). It has no number, so it is held as a non-numeric count, the same as 'few'.
A compound of two shape values. The playbook models it as a continuum between lanceolate and subulate.
Almost always describes hairs ('nonglandular hairs'), so it is 'not glandular' on the trichome. When the stated bearer is an organ, the trichome is the real bearer.
This means having many close, fine, parallel veins that give a striped look. That is the parallel venation PATO calls parallelodromous.
This means without a keel. It negates carinate, which the earlier rule C221 maps to keel-shaped.
This means slightly cordate: the approximate-value pattern applied to heart shaped, just as 'suborbicular' is handled.
Radially symmetric flowers are actinomorphic. PATO_0001325 radial symmetry is only the attribute, not a value.

label: anadromous
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the first segment or vein of each division of the bearer arising on the acroscopic side, towards the apex of the frond. NOTE: Fern-specific; the opposite is catadromous.
reason: A standard term in fern descriptions with no PATO or FLOPO equivalent. It describes the order of pinnules and veins along a pinna.
Globoid means ball-shaped, which is spherical (globular is an exact synonym).

label: cyme-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's architecture resembling a cyme, a determinate inflorescence whose main axis ends in a flower and whose later flowers arise on lateral branches below it. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002455 corymb-like and FLOPO:0991199 thyrse-like.
reason: Floras use 'cymiform arrays' for the form of an inflorescence. This matches the raceme-, panicle- and thyrse-like classes added in the previous review.
Same as ecarinate: the negation of carinate, which is keel-shaped.

label: autotrophic
definition: A trophic quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its obtaining its carbon by its own photosynthesis, without depending on a host plant or on fungi. NOTE: Contrasts with mycoheterotrophic and parasitic; possibly outside PATO's scope, like FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic.
reason: Orchid floras state it to contrast with mycoheterotrophic or leafless taxa. PATO has only the trophic quality attribute, not this value.
Voluble means twining. The climbing class already covers growing upwards by twining round a support, so an existing term is better than a narrower new one.

label: distylous
definition: A heterostylous quality inhering in a flower or plant by virtue of its belonging to a species whose flowers occur in two morphs, one with long styles and short stamens and one with short styles and long stamens. NOTE: Sibling of tristylous.
reason: The most common kind of heterostyly, especially in Rubiaceae. It is narrower than heterostylous, and that difference is botanically meaningful.
A compound of two shape values, modelled as a continuum.

label: scape-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to a scape: an elongate, leafless or nearly leafless flowering axis arising from the base of the plant. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like.
reason: This describes a stem or peduncle that looks like a scape. The bearer is not a scape (the scape rule maps to peduncle), so it is a resemblance quality, like bract-like.
Juxtaposed thecae, ovules or fruits are side by side and close together without being joined, which is the approximate class. It is said of a set of like parts, so it does not need a second term.
A compound of two shapes. PATO lance-ovate (PATO_0002337) is flat, while this is solid, so the continuum is safer.

label: septate
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being divided internally by transverse walls or partitions into a row of compartments. NOTE: 'nonseptate' is annotated as not septate; for hairs, nonseptate also implies PATO:0001994 unicellular.
reason: Said of hairs, Sphagnum hyaline cells and Juncus stems or leaves. PATO and FLOPO have no 'septate' value, and PO septum is the ovary or fruit partition, so neither a negation nor an absence rule has a target.
This means a life span that is relatively high, just as 'tall' was mapped to increased height.
The negation of the existing saccate class.

label: gonioautoicous
definition: An autoicous quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its male gametoecia being bud-like and borne in leaf axils on the same stem as, and usually just below, the female gametoecia. NOTE: Sibling of rhizautoicous and cladautoicous.
reason: A standard term for the sexual condition of mosses and a defined subtype of the existing autoicous class.
A part that does not persist is shed. PATO has no 'persistent' value, and deciduous (generic) is the disposition to shed parts. The bearer is the part that is shed.
A count of veins without a number (nerved → vein in flora_counted_parts). It is held as a non-numeric count, like 'few'.
Moderate-sized means of medium size for its kind, which is the existing medium-sized class.

label: bud-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to a bud: small, compact, and with its leaves or bracts closely overlapping. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like.
reason: Moss floras use it for perigonia and male buds. No PATO or FLOPO term covers this shape.
The French spelling of plano-convex, which is already a class.
This means bearing glands. Gland is a synonym of 'portion of secretory tissue' (as in rule C265).

There is no 'ranked' quality to negate ('ranked' was rejected earlier), and the count pattern does not split ranks. Phrases like 'unranked to 5-ranked' need a future number-of-ranks pattern, not a new term.
